Each transport words these for its own reader, which is why they live here and not in a shared library, and why changing them here changes nothing the MCP transport says about the same specs.

Raises:

Type Description ImproperlyConfigured

A field uses a placeholder it does not accept, is not a valid format string, is neither a string nor None, or is missing_arguments set to None or to an empty or whitespace-only string.

docs.title: base class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
base: str | None = (
    "The following tools call this application's services and selectors.
- A successful call returns the tool's data. A business-rule failure comes back as a failed call whose content is a sentence explaining why — that is a final answer, not a reason to retry; read it and report it, do not call the same tool the same way again. The sentence may end with `(code: <name>)`, naming the rule that refused; it is the same code an item's `affordances` answer carries when a tool advertised one.
- An invalid or missing argument comes back as a retry request naming the problem; correct the argument and call again.
- A permission error is final: the current user may not perform that call — do not retry it.
- Only pass documented parameters; unknown arguments are rejected."
)

The opening of the instructions block, said whatever the tools are.

Unconditional because the failure contract it states holds for every tool, and because no spec can answer whether a refusal will carry a (code: <name>): a declared Affordance produces one, and so does a service raising ActionUnavailable by hand, which nothing declares. No placeholders.

It names no framework: which library declared a tool is nothing a model can act on, and the line is read on every step.

docs.title: pagination class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
pagination: str | None = (
    "- Read-only tools that return a collection always return one page, shaped {envelope}. They accept optional `limit` (items per page, default {page_size}) and `page` (1-based). When `hasNext` is true there are more items than you were shown: ask for the next `page`, or narrow the request with a filter — never answer as if the page were the whole collection."
)

The block's line on pages, when some tool returns one.

{page_size} is the page an omitted limit is served, the same number each tool's limit description states, so the model is not told one default here and another on the tool.

{envelope} is the page written as an object, {"items": [...], "page": 1, "totalPages": N, "hasNext": true|false}, with "total": T last when the toolset is built with include_total. Off, the default says what it said before the placeholder existed, byte for byte.

docs.title: ordering class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
ordering: str | None = (
    "- Some collection tools also accept {names}. It takes exactly one of the values listed in that tool's schema (a sortable name, or the same name prefixed with `-` for descending) — not a comma-separated list, and not an arbitrary column."
)

The block's line on sorting, when some tool advertises a sort argument.

{names} is every sort argument the tools advertise, each in backticks and joined with ", ": the name is the project's to choose, and one toolset can carry tools whose sorts are declared under different names.

docs.title: handles class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
handles: str | None = (
    "- Some tools return opaque identifier fields, described as such in the tool's output. Pass them to other tools that ask for one; refer to records by their name in anything you say, never by the identifier."
)

The block's line on opaque identifiers, when some tool's output marks one.

The block-level half of handle_field_description. No placeholders.

docs.title: read_shaping class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
read_shaping: str | None = (
    "- Some tools accept read-shaping parameters ({names}) that adjust the shape of the returned data without filtering it."
)

The block's line on read-shaping parameters, when some tool has one.

A read-shaping parameter is one of the spec's shapes, which no callable of the spec takes and its presenter reads instead; one a selector or provider takes, by name or through **kwargs, is that callable's argument and is not named here. {names} is every such name, sorted, backticked, joined with ", ". None drops the line and read_shaping_on_pages with it, since that sentence continues this one.

docs.title: read_shaping_on_pages class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
read_shaping_on_pages: str | None = (
    "On a tool that returns a page, they apply to each item in `items`, never to the page itself."
)

Appended to read_shaping, after a space, when some tool that returns a page has a read-shaping parameter.

The block-level half of query_param_on_pages. {envelope} is the envelope's keys, as query_param_on_pages receives them. The default names no key, and so says the same whether or not the page carries total.

docs.title: unavailable_heading class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
unavailable_heading: str | None = (
    "- These operations exist but cannot be performed right now, so they are not among your tools. If the user asks for one, say it is unavailable at the moment and give the reason listed for it, rather than guessing why:"
)

The heading of the per-step list of operations an unmet condition left out.

Followed by one line per such tool, its name and its reason, and said only on a step that left one out. It is appended after an instructions= override as well, so it is the one block line that override does not replace. None drops the heading and the list beneath it. No placeholders.

docs.title: handle_field_description class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
handle_field_description: str | None = (
    "An opaque identifier. Pass it to other tools that ask for one; refer to the record by its name in anything you say, never by this value."
)

The description of a handle field in a tool's output schema, when the field's own marking declares none.

The kernel supplies no wording for a handle on purpose: what a reader should do with an identifier depends on the reader. No placeholders.

docs.title: query_param_on_pages class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
query_param_on_pages: str | None = (
    "On a paged result it applies to each item in `items`, never to the page envelope ({envelope})."
)

What a read-shaping parameter applies to on a tool that returns a page.

Appended after a space to each read-shaping parameter's description on such a tool, or its whole description when it declares none, and to the retry a render-time rejection on such a tool produces.

{envelope} is the envelope's keys, each in backticks and joined with ", ": items, page, totalPages and hasNext, then total when the toolset is built with include_total.

The envelope is the likeliest target for a bad selection because it is exactly the shape the tool documents returning -- {items{id, name}} is a natural reading of it -- while the presenter that reads the param only ever sees one row. Saying so at the parameter, where the model is choosing a value, turns that mistake into one retry.

docs.title: missing_arguments class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
missing_arguments: str = 'Missing required argument(s): {names}.'

The retry for a call that left out an argument it cannot run without.

Covers both checks made before the input serializer runs: a parameter the selector requires, and one of the spec's reads declared required. A field the input requires is reported by the spec's Validator, in its own words. {names} is every missing name, sorted, each in backticks and joined with ", ". Never None, empty or only whitespace: it is the retry's whole text.

docs.title: AGENT_TRANSPORT module-attribute
docs.text:
AGENT_TRANSPORT: Final = 'agent'

The value of call_context["transport"] on every call a SpecToolset serves.

This package's own spelling: the kernel lists no transports, so each transport package owns and exports its value. It is the plain string, so a spec callable written for several transports compares call_context["transport"] == "agent" with nothing imported, and one written for agents alone may import this name instead. The toolset stamps it last, through the kernel's build_call_context, over any transport entry the run's own context carries.

docs.title: testing
docs.text: Test doubles for driving a toolset through a real Agent run loop. See Running from a worker.

docs.title: testing
docs.text:
Test doubles for driving a toolset through a real Agent run loop.

Asserting on call_tool directly answers does the tool work. It does not answer the questions that only the run loop can: that the tools execute in-process rather than being deferred to the client, that a ModelRetry is fed back for another attempt instead of aborting, that the toolset's get_instructions actually reaches the model. Those need an Agent, and an Agent needs a model.

FunctionModel is the model with no provider and no network behind it, and the recipes here are the ones a consumer wanting the same coverage would otherwise re-derive from the pydantic-ai docs.

Test doubles, not fixtures. Nothing here touches Django, the database or pytest, so it composes with whatever a project already uses.

Pydantic-AI is the only thing it imports, which is why it sits at the package's top level rather than under spec_tools: a host-only install, with no [specs] extra and no Django REST Framework, can drive its own agents with these doubles. The package root never imports it.

from pydantic_ai import Agent
from django_spec_agents import AgentDeps
from django_spec_agents.spec_tools import SpecToolset
from django_spec_agents.testing import tool_calling_model

agent = Agent(tool_calling_model("list_widgets"), deps_type=AgentDeps, toolsets=[toolset])
result = await agent.run("go", deps=AgentDeps(user=user))

docs.title: tool_calling_model
docs.text:
tool_calling_model(
    tool_name: str,
    args: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    *,
    retry_args: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    final_text: str = "done",
) -> FunctionModel

A model that calls one tool, optionally corrects itself once, then stops.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default tool_name str

The tool to call. It must be one the toolset advertises -- an unknown name is a retry from the tool manager, not a failure the model sees, so the run fails with "exceeded max retries" once that tool's retry budget is spent.

required args Mapping[str, Any] | None

The arguments for the first call.

None retry_args Mapping[str, Any] | None

The arguments for the second call, used only if the first raised ModelRetry. Defaults to args, which makes the model repeat itself -- fine for asserting the retry reached it, and wrong for asserting recovery, since a spec that rejected those arguments once will reject them again and the run will not settle.

None final_text str

The output once a tool call has returned.

'done'

Returns:

Type Description FunctionModel

A FunctionModel: no provider, no network, no key.

The branch order matters and is not arbitrary. A retry is checked before a tool return, because from pydantic-ai 2.60 a retried call is a tool return, marked outcome="retried", and the tool-return arm would end the run on the failed attempt. Below 2.60 the retry is a separate retry-prompt part, and both shapes are read.

docs.title: streaming_tool_calling_model
docs.text:
streaming_tool_calling_model(
    tool_name: str,
    args: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    *,
    retry_args: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    final_text: str = "done",
) -> FunctionModel

tool_calling_model, for a transport that streams.

The arguments and the behaviour are that function's; the difference is that this one supplies stream_function as well, and it exists because a FunctionModel built with function= alone cannot serve a streamed request at all -- it raises FunctionModel must receive a `stream_function` to support streamed requests.

That matters more than a missing convenience. AG-UI always streams, so a consumer reaching for the double next door to test what its browser receives gets a run that dies before the toolset is touched -- and the transport redacts the reason, so what reaches the client is "The run failed", naming nothing.

Both functions are supplied, which FunctionModel allows: the same double then serves a streamed run and a non-streamed one, so a test does not have to know which the transport under it chose.

from django_spec_agents.testing import streaming_tool_calling_model

# An AG-UI endpoint, driven end to end.
agent = Agent(streaming_tool_calling_model("refund_order", {"reference": "ENC-1"}))

docs.title: instruction_capturing_model
docs.text:
instruction_capturing_model(
    captured: dict[str, Any], *, final_text: str = "done"
) -> FunctionModel

A model that records the instructions it was given and calls nothing.

Writes captured["instructions"] on every request, so the last value is what the final request carried.

The caller owns the dict rather than getting one back with the model, because the assertion happens after agent.run returns and a tuple return reads worse at every call site than a name that is already in scope:

captured: dict[str, Any] = {}
agent = Agent(instruction_capturing_model(captured), toolsets=[toolset])
await agent.run("go", deps=deps)
assert "Sort with" in captured["instructions"]

A toolset's get_instructions is collected by pydantic-ai rather than by anything here, so this is the only way to assert the conventions a SpecToolset contributes actually arrive -- and they arrive on the request, not on the toolset.

docs.title: slow_model
docs.text:
slow_model(delay: float, chunks: Sequence[str] = ('done',)) -> FunctionModel

A model that answers chunks after delay seconds; streamed, all but the last first.

For a run's timeout=: the wait is in the request, where a provider's is, and the double never raises TimeoutError itself, so a RunTimedOut is the run's deadline and nothing else. Streamed, every chunk but the last arrives before the wait, so a timed-out run keeps them as its partial response, as it does when a provider's stream stalls mid-answer.

from pydantic_ai.exceptions import RunTimedOut
from django_spec_agents.testing import slow_model

agent = Agent(slow_model(10.0))
with pytest.raises(RunTimedOut):
    await agent.run("go", timeout=0.05)

docs.title: Declaring specs once, across transports
docs.text:
If the agent is the only place your project exposes its specs, keep passing a plain dict — this page buys you nothing.

It pays off when the same specs are also exposed elsewhere: over MCP with django-spec-mcp, or as ordinary HTTP views. Each transport has to be told which specs it exposes, so the list gets written once per transport and the copies drift — a spec is added to the MCP wiring and forgotten in the agent's, or the same operation is named create_order in one place and something else in the other.

SpecRegistry is the one declaration site. SpecToolset and SpecCapability accept one anywhere they accept a mapping — there is no separate constructor to learn.

docs.title: Declare once
docs.text:
# orders/registry.py
from django_service_specs import SpecRegistry

registry = SpecRegistry()


# orders/apps.py
from django.apps import AppConfig


class OrdersConfig(AppConfig):
    name = "orders"

    def ready(self) -> None:
        from orders import specs
        from orders.registry import registry

        registry.register("list_orders", specs.list_orders, tags=("read", "public"))
        registry.register("refund_order", specs.refund_order, tags=("write", "admin"))

docs.title: Hand it to the agent
docs.text:
from pydantic_ai import Agent

from django_spec_agents import AgentDeps
from django_spec_agents.spec_tools import SpecToolset
from orders.registry import registry

agent = Agent(model, deps_type=AgentDeps, toolsets=[SpecToolset(registry)])

That is the whole change. Each entry becomes one tool, named as it is in the registry, in registration order.

The registry is django-service-specs', and it accepts any spec that compiles to one of the kernel's, and so does the toolset: a django-service-specs ServiceSpec or SelectorSpec, or any value the kernel's kernel_spec compiles to one. The toolset reads every spec through kernel_spec, so it asks the compiled spec what to advertise and how to call it, whichever library declared it. A value that compiles to no spec raises TypeError naming the tool when the toolset is built, in the kernel's words.

docs.title: A spec declared on the kernel
docs.text:
A django-service-specs spec needs no DRF. Its permissions are the kernel's PermissionChecks, and its arguments are its declared reads: the kernel reflects nothing off a native callable's signature, so each argument the model may send is a Parameter, and the callable takes it by name beside the pool seeds (user here). A native spec declaring no reads advertises no argument of its own, and a call sending one is handed back as name: Unknown argument.

from django_service_specs import (
    Parameter,
    Parameters,
    PermissionCheck,
    SelectorKind,
    SelectorSpec,
    ServiceSpec,
)

from django_spec_agents.spec_tools import SpecToolset
from orders.models import Order


class SignedIn(PermissionCheck):
    def has_permission(self, principal, spec) -> bool:
        return bool(principal is not None and principal.is_authenticated)


def orders_in_status(*, user, status: str) -> list[dict]:
    """The caller's orders in one status."""
    return list(Order.objects.filter(owner=user, status=status).values("id", "status"))


def set_order_note(*, user, pk: int, note: str) -> dict:
    """Write the note on one of the caller's orders."""
    Order.objects.filter(owner=user, pk=pk).update(note=note)
    return {"id": pk, "note": note}


list_orders = SelectorSpec(
    kind=SelectorKind.LIST,
    selector=orders_in_status,
    reads=Parameters.of(Parameter("status", "string", default="open")),
    permissions=[SignedIn()],
)
note_order = ServiceSpec(
    service=set_order_note,
    reads=Parameters.of(
        Parameter("pk", "integer", required=True),
        Parameter("note", "string", required=True),
    ),
    permissions=[SignedIn()],
)

toolset = SpecToolset({"list_orders": list_orders, "note_order": note_order})

list_orders advertises status, defaulting to open, beside the page and limit every list tool takes, and returns a page of the dicts its selector returns. note_order requires pk and note. A registry takes these specs as it takes any other, and the toolset serves them from either.

docs.title: A registry or its mapping
docs.text:
SpecToolset(registry) and SpecToolset(registry.specs()) build the same tools: the mapping is the flattened name -> spec view, and everything the toolset reads is on the spec. Pass the registry when you have one, so a filtered view of it can feed each toolset.

The same goes for the capability:

from django_spec_agents.spec_tools import SpecCapability

AgentConfig(capabilities=[SpecCapability(registry)])

docs.title: Project several toolsets from one declaration
docs.text:
by_tag and subset each return a new registry holding a snapshot, so one declaration site can feed several toolsets with no shared state:

reads = SpecToolset(registry.by_tag("read"), id="reads")
admin = SpecToolset(registry.by_tag("admin"), id="admin")

agent = Agent(model, deps_type=AgentDeps, toolsets=[reads, admin])

With capabilities, give each its own id — the id keys defer_loading's catalog entry, so two capabilities sharing one would collide:

AgentConfig(
    capabilities=[
        SpecCapability(
            registry.by_tag("read"),
            id="reads",
            description="Read-only order and customer lookups.",
        ),
        SpecCapability(
            registry.by_tag("admin"),
            id="admin",
            description="Account administration: suspend, refund, reassign.",
            defer_loading=True,
        ),
    ]
)

Here defer_loading hides the admin tools behind Pydantic-AI's native load_capability tool until the model asks for them — worth doing when the admin surface is large and rarely needed.

Give every deferred capability a description. It is the line the model picks from: the catalog renders - {id}: {description} when there is one and a bare - {id} when there is not, so a few undescribed capabilities leave the model choosing between names alone — and it will either guess or load all of them, which is the cost deferring was meant to avoid. description names the capability; the separate descriptions mapping relabels individual tools.

docs.title: What the spec declares for an agent
docs.text:
A spec declares what a caller with no HTTP request has to be told, because the URLconf and query string tell an HTTP one for free: reads= names the route captures and query values it reads, and an OutputField's marking= says how the field is presented to an agent. Both are the spec's: each read is one of its parameters, and the markings are part of its output.

from dataclasses import replace

from django_service_specs import Parameter, Parameters

registry.register(
    "list_orders",
    replace(
        specs.list_orders,
        reads=Parameters.of(Parameter("tenant_pk", "integer", required=True)),
        shapes=Parameters.of(Parameter("fields", "string")),
    ),
    tags=("read", "public"),
)

replace is for a spec declared elsewhere; a spec you write declares reads= and shapes= in its own constructor. SpecRegistry.register takes no contract of its own: the spec is the one place it is said.

SpecToolset reads them off the compiled spec, and an MCP server's register_specs reads the same spec. That is the point of putting them there: an operation needs the identical description of the absent request whichever agent transport calls it, which is why a toolset takes no channel declarations of its own: SpecToolset has no query_params=, tool_query_params=, url_kwargs= or tool_url_kwargs=, and passing one is a TypeError. A field's marking is part of the spec's output declaration, so every projection of the spec carries it, whichever transport or mapping it is reached through.

A registry and registry.specs() build the same tools. The tool's schema is the compiled spec's, the spec's reads are advertised, a read's default reaches a call that leaves it out or sends null, and a value the model sends under one of those names is admitted and handed to the spec as the kernel hands any caller's. A read declared required=True and sent as null is handed back as name: This field is required., the kernel's check. A read declared required=True with a default is not refused: the default answers a call that leaves it out, as the kernel reads it. A native read declared nullable keeps a null sent under it as the value.

Every read the spec declares is checked against the pool seeds when the toolset is built, whichever source it came from: a read named after a registered seed, at the top level or on a service's target lookup, is refused there, naming the tool, and so is a many spec whose list (many_argument) is named after a registered seed or after request or view, which each call registers. A parameter in shapes=, which no callable takes, may not be named page, limit or ordering, which a list tool takes for itself. A read named ordering that a callable takes is an argument like any other, advertised and left in the call.

docs.title: Arguments the server supplies
docs.text:
Some arguments are not the model's to choose. An agent run scoped to one project should not be able to list another project's rows by sending a different project_pk, and a model asked for an identifier it cannot know tends to invent one or send the parameter's name. tool_server_arguments answers for such names per tool, with django-service-specs' ServerArguments:

from django_service_specs import ServerArguments

toolset = SpecToolset(
    registry,
    tool_server_arguments={
        "list_document_vendors": ServerArguments(
            values={"project_pk": str(document.project_id)},
            withheld=frozenset({"draw_request_pk"}),
        ),
    },
)
  • A bound name (values) carries the server's value on every call. It satisfies a required parameter, and every reader of the call sees the one value: a kwargs= provider taking its name is handed it, and the selector receives it as its parameter.
  • A withheld name is absent from every call, so the read's declared default, or the callable's own, answers. Withholding the other names of an either-or scope is how a tool taking a project or a draw request is held to the project.
  • Neither is advertised. Both leave the tool's properties and required, and the instructions name neither. If the model sends one anyway, its value is dropped before the call is checked, never refused, so a guess costs no retry, and the toolset logs the tool and the names at WARNING, never the values.

Each name must be one the tool's spec declares: a selector or target-lookup parameter, or one of its reads. The toolset checks every binding when it is built, with django-service-specs' check_server_arguments and the toolset's own pool_seeds, and raises ImproperlyConfigured naming the tool for a name the spec does not declare, a name a pool seed or a typed kwargs= provider fills, a withheld name no call could do without, or a bound value its parameter refuses. A key naming a tool the toolset does not expose raises ValueError, as every per-tool mapping does.

The mount's pool_seeds are all that check can see. A seed a call_seeds override returns under a bound or withheld read or parameter is refused at the call instead, by the same check with the call's seeds, with ImproperlyConfigured naming the tool. It is a configuration error and not a retry, since the seed would otherwise win over the server's value without a trace. A bound Validator field of the same name is not refused, here or on the mount: the field takes the bound value and the service parameter the seed.

Those checks read the spec as described to no call, where the tool's schema reads it under the agent's stamp, so binding a field declared only to the agent is refused as undeclared. A Validator declaring parameters(self, *, call_context=None) can declare a bound field otherwise to a call, so every call checks the bound values again, against what the Validator declares to that call. One its declaration refuses raises ImproperlyConfigured naming the tool and the spec, never a retry, since the model neither sent the value nor can see it.

The bindings are fixed when the toolset is built, like its tool definitions. For a per-run scope, build a toolset per run, from the run's scope. A tool counts as scoped by the run only when the run binds one of the scope names it reads: its other optional scope reads are then withheld too, so the model cannot widen the scope through a sibling, while a required one the run does not bind stays the model's to send, since withheld no call could supply it. A tool reading only scope names the run does not bind gets no binding and keeps them all:

SCOPE_NAMES = frozenset({"project_pk", "draw_request_pk", "document_pk"})


def scope_bindings(registry, scope):
    """Each tool the run's scope reaches: the bound names, and optional siblings withheld."""
    bindings = {}
    for entry in registry.all():
        reads = [read for read in entry.spec.reads if read.name in SCOPE_NAMES]
        values = {read.name: scope[read.name] for read in reads if read.name in scope}
        if not values:
            continue
        bindings[entry.name] = ServerArguments(
            values=values,
            # A required read stays the model's: withheld, no call could supply it.
            withheld=frozenset(
                read.name for read in reads if read.name not in values and not read.required
            ),
        )
    return bindings


toolset = SpecToolset(registry, tool_server_arguments=scope_bindings(registry, scope))

SpecCapability takes the same keyword.

docs.title: What stays per toolset
docs.text: The rest of SpecToolset's signature, because it is genuinely this mount's: get_user, unknown_arguments, max_retries, the result-size and page ceilings. A publicly exposed MCP endpoint and an in-process toolset carry different risk, so one shared number would be a regression rather than a simplification.

docs.title: Moving a channel declaration off the toolset
docs.text: A toolset that declared a read at the mount declares it on the spec instead, as reads= and shapes= (see what the spec declares for an agent). A read's default is only a default: the model can override it, and it stays advertised. To keep a value the model should not choose, use tool_server_arguments.

docs.title: Names
docs.text: Registry names are free-form, but tool names are not: model providers constrain them to [a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}. A registry name outside that shape raises when the toolset is built, rather than failing later at the provider boundary. If you share a registry with a transport that has looser naming, keep the names tool-safe.
